fields.v: Metrics: F1 / EM% / SQL valid% / AST exact% / AST sim / runnable%; models not stated for Stage 2. fields.quote: 4. Immediate Runnability. Percentage of generated scripts that could execute without additional manual modifications in the experimental database environment.
fields.why: The verdicts (works / partly / does not work) rest on thresholds chosen by the extractor: the authors define the six metrics without any success threshold, so per the 2026-11-23 rule each configuration should read 'no criterion stated by the authors'.
fields.doubt: Os autores definem as métricas (pág. 7) mas não dão nenhum limiar de sucesso; os veredictos 'Partly', 'Does not work' e 'cost works' foram decididos por quem extraiu. Pela regra de 23-11, troca-os por 'no criterion stated by the authors' (como fizeste no OpenHarmony Bench).

fields.v: Spec-first (not classified by the authors; specification generated first and code derived from it, both in the Stage 1 pipeline and in the native Kiro / Spec Kit / Antigravity flows). Authors' wording: 'specification-first migration pipeline', 'specification-first approach'
fields.quote: First, a specification-first migration pipeline was evaluated on 1,006 PL/SQL files, of which 623 were successfully regenerated and 380 generated scripts executed successfully in PostgreSQL 16.
fields.why: 'Not stated' is not one of the allowed levels (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source, not classifiable), and the authors themselves call the pipeline 'specification-first'.
fields.doubt: 'Not stated' não é um dos níveis do protocolo. Os autores chamam ao pipeline 'specification-first' (pág. 1 e conclusão, pág. 10). Decide entre Spec-first e Not classifiable e mantém a expressão dos autores.
